    "reading": "A place of rocking or swaying at a sharp extremity; a threshold between stability and motion.",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "Middle English Dictionary (MED), Lewis & Short Latin Dictionary",

  {

    "chain": "Roker → roc + cœur (French homophone of 'cœur' = heart); Point → pointe (French = point, tip)",
    "reading": "The rock-heart's tip: a stony core that pierces, a heart made mineral.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.7
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Roker (English) ~ rocher (French = rock) ~ roka (Swedish = rook, chess piece); Point ~ pointe (French) ~ punto (Italian)",
    "reading": "A chess rook's point: a move of power at the edge of the board, a strategic extremity.",
    "languages": ["en", "fr", "sv", "it"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Roker Point → 'Porter Koin' (koin = Greek for common, shared); also 'Ripe Torok' (Torok = Turkish for throat)",
    "reading": "A common throat: a shared passage or voice, a point where many speak as one.",
    "languages": ["en", "grc", "tr"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "Roker Point → R.P. → Rota Punctum (Latin: wheel's point) or Regula Puncti (rule of the point)",
    "reading": "The wheel's pivot: the fixed centre around which all turning occurs, the still axis.",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "R (res, Latin = thing) + O (omega, end) + K (kaph, Hebrew = palm) + E (epsilon, breath) + R (again); Point = P (pater, father) + T (tau, cross)",
    "reading": "Thing, end, palm, breath, father, cross: a hand that holds the end of breath at the cross.",
    "languages": ["la", "grc", "he"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "R=18, O=15, K=11, E=5, R=18 → sum 67; Point: P=16, O=15, I=9, N=14, T=20 → sum 74; 67+74=141; 1+4+1=6",
    "reading": "Six: the number of balance and harmony, a point that resolves into the hexad of creation.",

    "source": "generative",

  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Roker (Old Norse raukr = stack, pillar of rock) + Point (Old French point, from Latin pungere = to prick)",
    "reading": "A pillar that pricks: a standing stone that wounds the sky, a vertical assertion.",
    "languages": ["en", "non", "fr", "la"],
    "source": "Cleasby-Vigfusson Old Norse Dictionary; OED",
    "confidence": 0.7
  }
